Subject: Monthly metrics cadence — leadership check-in (latency / cost / uptime / usage)

Hi team,

Attaching the June dashboard (monthly_kpi_dash_2028-06.pdf) and a quick CSV extract for the latency tails (latency-95p-breakdown.csv). High level flags before our Friday QBR dry run:

- Latency: 95p for embeddings up ~18ms month-over-month in prod-us-west-2; coincides with the larger batch arrival pattern from the beta integration (Acme).
- Cost: normalized cost per 1k tokens climbed ~4% driven by more small random inference calls (cold-starts + suboptimal batching).
- Uptime: rolling 30d uptime dropped from 99.93% -> 99.86% due to two short restarts during an infra maintenance window in ap-south-1; we surfaced region failover behavior but saw a small queue buildup.
- Usage: daily active client count +17% driven by Acme pilot; peak concurrency increased ~22% during their morning window (11:00–13:00 PDT).

Ask: please review the attachments and call out any blockers/asks for the QBR slide deck (I started a draft: qbr-slide-draft.pptx). Specific owners below — flag if you'd like to swap.

Proposed owners / asks:
- Olga: dig into root cause for embeddings 95p bump and whether kernel selection changed after the last runtime patch.
- Markus: confirm cost model on the new beta traffic pattern and estimate impact of enabling prefix caching for that tenant.
- Karthik: synthesize the outage timeline and customer-facing impact (we need an internal blameless postmortem ready).
- Laura: consolidate exec one-pager and a single-slide recommendation (3 bullets) for the QBR.

Timeline: please post initial replies by EOD Thu (6/23) so we can lock slides Thu evening.

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: monthly_kpi_dash_2028-06.pdf (PDF, 14 pages); latency-95p-breakdown.csv (CSV, 82 rows); qbr-slide-draft.pptx (PPTX, draft)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Monthly metrics cadence — leadership check-in (latency / cost / uptime / usage)

Sean —

Quick update after a first-pass run of the 95p traces:
- The bump correlates with a kernel fallback we deployed 2028-06-03 to address a rare OOM in the llama-embed path. Fallback keeps correctness but increases single-token latency for longer sequences due to processing on a compatibility kernel.
- The Acme traffic pattern (more frequent small batch requests) increases overhead because we aren't hitting the continuous batching thresholds.

Immediate mitigation options (short list):
1) Revert the compatibility kernel for the embed op in us-west-2 (fast but risk reintroducing the rare OOM) — Rollback window required.
2) Force micro-batching for the Acme tenant at the routing layer to coalesce small requests for 30s windows (medium complexity).
3) Enable additional warm spin-up samples for embeddings on dedicated nodes serving that tenant (costly).

I'll run a microbench with the prior kernel on a canary pool and post numbers by Thu morning. If numbers look good we can propose a narrowly scoped rollback for the QBR recommendation.

- Olga
Olga Petrov
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

1) Impact summary (1 line): "Monthly cost +4%; latency 95p +18ms for embeddings driven by kernel fallback and smaller batch sizes from one pilot tenant; uptime marginal impact from two brief region restarts."
2) Risk & mitigation (2 lines): "Risk: sustained small-request traffic may raise unit costs and impact SLAs. Mitigations: tenant-specific batching + canary rollback of embed kernel; dedicated warmers if required."
3) Ask (1 line): "Approve canary rollback window (3h) for us-west-2 pending Olga's microbench and a targeted tenant routing change."

I've left an explicit owner column and a 'QBR ask' checkbox. Two items for leadership: approve rollback contingency and authorize a small pilot for tenant-level batching.

One open question: do we want to include the short uptime blip with the timeline, or fold into infra improvements? My recommendation: include it as an operational note with a single-sentence remediation (improved maintenance migration policy).

Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations
